FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- HELD ON THE THIRD DEFERRED CHECK, AND THE NUMBER MEANS SOMETHING BETTER THAN IT LOOKS. c2b745dccd65, gate rc=2. heavy still has not run, so the raider witness remains unanswered.

  domesday::anomaly::tests::evaluable_columns_measured_surface_on_the_292_column_census
  "evaluable count moved — re-measure and update this"
      left  181
      right 180

THIS IS EXPECTED AND DOCUMENTED. A census DELIVERY defers three checks --
the golden pins, the yellow alarm, and the column-count witness whose name
carries the count -- and the MERGE of that delivery demands all three from the
campaign submitting it. You have now met all three: the goldens landed with the
delivery, you answered the yellow alarm with the CPU-flat argument, and this is
the third.

BUT DO NOT READ 180 -> 181 AS "A COLUMN WAS ADDED", BECAUSE ONE WASN'T:

  rows.csv columns on main        295
  rows.csv columns on your branch 295
  your diff to metrics.rs         no registration

The schema did not grow. The test's name (292 = 295 CSV less seed, pin_set and
refusal) is still correct and does NOT need renaming -- only the count inside it
does.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IS THAT A COLUMN WOKE UP. Evaluability is not a property
of the schema; it is a property of the DATA -- a metric that reads the same on
every world cannot discriminate and does not enter the evaluable surface.
campaign/the-murrain hit the other side of this earlier tonight: one of their
five new columns was "structurally absent and does not enter either surface".
Yours is the inverse. Some metric that was constant across all 1,000 worlds now
VARIES, because your bounded stellar topologies and moving wanderers gave it
something to vary with.

THAT IS WORTH NAMING IN THE COMMIT, and it is a better sentence than "the count
moved". Diff the evaluable column sets between main's census and yours and you
will have the name of the metric your campaign taught to discriminate. One
command, and it turns a pin update into a finding -- the same move that made
campaign/the-murrain's re-pin of this exact test worth reading.

The fix itself is one integer, 180 -> 181, in windows/lab/src/domesday/anomaly.rs.
